title: Read which data elements a bitmap says are present

blocks.text: The receiving side of a link never sees your `ISOMsg`: it sees bytes, and the bitmap is how it learns which data elements follow. Reading it wrongly shifts every field after the mistake, so the whole message parses as nonsense.
Write `BitmapReader.present(String bitmapHex)`. It takes the bitmap part of a message as hexadecimal digits (either case) and returns, in ascending order, every data element it says is present.

items: The first sixteen digits are the primary bitmap. Bit *n*, counted from 1, most significant first, stands for data element *n*, from 2 to 64.

Bit 1 of the primary bitmap is not a data element. When it is set, a secondary bitmap of sixteen more digits follows, and its bit *n* stands for data element 64 + *n*, from 65 to 128. Only the primary's bit 1 is a flag: there is no tertiary bitmap here.
The length must agree with bit 1: sixteen digits when it is clear, thirty-two when it is set. Anything else, including a digit that is not hexadecimal, is refused with an `IllegalArgumentException`.

cases.says: lists, in ascending order, every data element the primary and any secondary bitmap flag
the secondary bitmap's first bit is data element 65, not another flag
a secondary bitmap must be there when bit 1 is set, and must not be there when it is clear

concepts: A receiver learns which data elements follow by reading the bitmap: a data element is present exactly when its bit is 1.
Data elements 65 to 128 are flagged in a secondary bitmap, which follows the primary one only when the primary's bit 1 is set.
